Question:
A bus takes \(2\) minutes to drive from one stop to the next, and waits \(1\) minute at each stop to let passengers board. Zia takes \(5\) minutes to walk from one bus stop to the next. As Zia reaches a bus stop, if the bus is at the previous stop or has already left the previous stop, then she will wait for the bus. Otherwise she will start walking toward the next stop. Suppose the bus and Zia start at the same time toward the library, with the bus \(3\) stops behind. After how many minutes will Zia board the bus?

[Figure 1](figures/2022_AMC_8_Q22_question_fig1.svg)
Solution:
Check the bus's position whenever Zia reaches a stop, because those are the moments when she decides whether to wait.

Number the bus's starting stop \(0\). Zia starts three stops ahead, at stop \(3\). The bus reaches stop \(1\) after \(2\) minutes and waits a minute before moving on. It therefore reaches stops \(2,3,4,5,6\) at minutes \(5,8,11,14,17\), with a one-minute wait at each.

Zia reaches stops \(4,5,6\) at minutes \(5,10,15\). At minute \(5\), the bus is at stop \(2\), so it has not reached her previous stop \(3\); she keeps walking. At minute \(10\), the bus is between stops \(3\) and \(4\). It has not reached her previous stop \(4\), so she keeps walking again.

At minute \(15\), Zia reaches stop \(6\) just as the bus leaves stop \(5\). She now waits, and it reaches her \(2\) minutes later. She boards at minute \(\boxed{17}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).
